source_excerpts.text:
## What remains constructive after compression

For an arbitrary original affine observation \(Q=q_0+W\), the compiler computes \(BQ\). Every nonempty original fiber
\[
Q\cap B^{-1}(y)
\]
has the same population
\[
\tau=|W\cap P(f)|.
\]

For a certified Boolean function, this gives three separate operations:

- **Count:** \(\tau\sum_{y\in BQ}g(y)\), evaluated by exact Gaussian sums.
- **Witness:** select an accepted quotient point and solve its actual original affine fiber.
- **Exact uniform sampling:** use a bijective integer index over accepted quotient points and their original fibers. One uniform integer produces one uniform accepted original, without rare-event rejection.

The inverse index solves coordinates in the actual fiber basis. Its order is quotient-first followed by fiber coordinates, rather than original numeric order.

Two quotient representations are implemented and reviewed. Averaging projected affine terms requires exact multiplicity factors; omitting them gives wrong answers when cancellation creates new periods. The equally informed alternative chooses an actual right inverse \(R\) of \(B\) and evaluates \(g(y)=f(Ry)\), using affine **preimages** with unchanged coefficients.

A decisive independent check excluded every selected section representative from the observation while retaining eight valid originals. All eight were still correctly counted, reconstructed and sampled. The section serves evaluation; conditioned output uses the full original fiber.

statement: For original Q=q0+W, every nonempty Q intersect B^-1(y) has population |W intersect P(f)|. The producer reports separate Boolean counts, witnesses and exact uniform bijective indexing of accepted quotient points and actual original fibers. A right inverse R evaluates g(y)=f(Ry); its section representatives need not lie in Q.
title: Use a quotient section only for evaluation and retain all conditioned originals
